chapter: New Orleans, Havana and back to New York
title: Other New York bands c. 1933-36: Casa Loma, Dorseys and Lunceford
summary: He lists Casa Loma, Claude Hopkins, Spitalny, Lopez and others, and tries to date the Glen Island Casino and Larchmont Casino engagements with Willard and Chilton.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: What other bands were playing in New York then, when you were there?

Well, at that time, let's see, the Casa Loma Band had come into the Roseland Ballroom and made quite a hit. Claude Hopkins' band was playing there also. And let's see, well, the inevitable Phil Spitalny and of course Freddie Martin, and Vincent Lopez. Let's see, I'm not sure, I think Hal Kemp was already gone from the Taft, but George Hall. And oh, there were -- this was before Shaw started his thing and it was before the Dorseys. The Dorseys, I think -- the Dorsey Brothers, that year, I think they came the following year, if I'm not mistaken, because Casa Loma was the -- I'm trying to remember who went into the Glenn Allen Casino first, whether it was the Dorsey Brothers or Casa Loma. Of course Casa Loma -- I'm inclined to think it might be the Casa Loma Band.
I think I have that somewhere in these notes, but I'll have to find it later.

Anyway, one of -- I'm sure the Casa Loma band didn't -- they may have gone in -- well, let's see, Jimmy Lunsford was around, too, although he wasn't -- the Cotton Club was still uptown, and I think he played there. I'm not sure. That was Harold Oxley's band. That was the one, the black band that the Mills organization didn't have. But yeah, -- let's see -- no, no, that's right, because Jimmy
Lunsford's band played opposite, they played at the Larchmont Casino when we played the Glenn Allen Casino, which was, I think, in '35, or '36.

Chilton has you going from -- let's see, the Paramount Hotel Grill in '33 to the following year, Park Central Hotel, '34, and then he says Glenn Allen Casino, Glen Island Hotel Roosevelt, New Orleans, et cetera.
